body.p: Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the present application in view of the
foregoing amendments and the reasons that follow.
No claims have been amended or canceled. No new matter has been added. Claims 1-12
and 21-28 remain pending in this application, with claims 10-12 being withdrawn. Applicant
respectfully requests reconsideration of these claims.
Applicant appreciates the courtesies extended to Applicant's undersigned representative
by Examiner Pruitt during the telephone interview on February 28, 2023 with the undersigned.
During the interview, the rejection of claim 1 under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as allegedly
being anticipated by EP 2357356 ("Katz") was discussed. Applicant's representatives argued that Katz does not disclose a pendulum mass structure with "a second end configured to rotate
freely about the pivot axis in accordance with a rotational speed of the rotor blade about the rotor
axis," as recited in claim 1. Instead, the "end proximate the mass 6" of Katz, which the Office
Action equated to the second end of the pendulum mass structure, is coupled to an actuator 5 that
"causes the mass [6] to move." (Katz [0013]). After further review, the Examiner agreed that the "end proximate the mass 6" of Katz is not "configured to rotate freely about the pivot axis in
accordance with a rotational speed of the rotor blade" as recited in claim 1.
In view of the recognition during the interview of Katz's deficiencies with respect to the
pending claims, it is respectfully requested that a new Office Action be issued should the
Examiner deem that the application is not in condition for allowance.
Claims 1-3 and 5-6 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as allegedly being
anticipated by EP 2357356 ("Katz").
As discussed above, claim 1 recites that the pendulum mass structure includes "a second

end configured to rotate freely about the pivot axis in accordance with a rotational speed of the rotor blade." However, as agreed during the interview, Katz does not teach this feature, at least because the "end proximate the mass 6" of Katz, which the Office Action equates to the second
end of the pendulum mass structure, is coupled to an actuator 5 that "causes the mass [6] to
move." (Katz [0013]). Paragraph [0014] of Katz further discloses that the "actuator is
preferably designed as an electrically, pneumatically or hydraulically operating actuator." Thus,
the mass 6 does not "rotate freely about the pivot axis" but rotates only upon actuation of the
actuator 5, "which drives the mass [6] directly." (Katz para. [0056]). Accordingly, Katz does
not teach or suggest, much less identically disclose, that a second end of a pendulum mass is
configured to "rotate freely about the pivot axis in accordance with a rotational speed of the rotor
blade," as recited in claim 1.
For at least these reasons, claim 1 is allowable over Katz. Claims 2, 3, 5, and 6 depend
from claim 1 and are allowable for at least the same reasons as claim 1, even without regard to
the further patentable features recited therein. Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the
Claims 7-9 and 28 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable
over Katz. As discussed above, claim 1 is allowable over Katz. Claims 7-9 and 28 depend from
claim 1 and are allowable for at least the same reasons as claim 1, even without regard to the
further patentable features recited therein.
Claim 4 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Katz in
view of U.S. Patent No. 5,639,214 ("Guimbal"). Claims 21-25 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. §
103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Katz in view of U.S. Patent No. 2,426,130 ("Wald").
Claims 4 and 21-28 depend from claim 1. Guimbal and Wald do not remedy the
deficiencies of Katz discussed above with respect to claim 1. Accordingly, claim 1 and its dependent claims, claims 4 and 21-28, are allowable over Katz, Guimbal, and Wald in any
combination.
Applicant appreciates the indication that claims 26-27 are allowable.
To the extent a requirement for restriction and/or election of species was made final in
this application, Applicant asserts that all pending claims other than those identified as
withdrawn, are either generic or read on the elected invention and/or species. Applicant intends
for this Reply to be fully responsive to the outstanding Office Action.
Applicant believes that the application is in condition for allowance. Favorable
reconsideration is respectfully requested. The Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned by
telephone if it is felt that a telephone interview would advance prosecution.
Respectfully submitted,
